groups.title: Paste (335400CPA)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the inflammation of chronic desquamative gingivitis and of intractable stomatitis and glossitis with erosion or ulceration.
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (the diseased site) once to several times a day. The amount may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have a tuberculous, viral or other purulent infection of the mouth, syphilis, chickenpox, a fungal infection or a bacterial skin infection; if you have perioral dermatitis or rosacea; or if you have gingivitis caused by vitamin C deficiency.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to propylene glycol or have had a reaction to it, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or if the user is a baby, a child or an older person.

Do not eat immediately after use. Do not use this medicine in the eyes.

Mild discomfort in the mouth such as numbness, abnormal or reduced taste, and a foreign-body sensation at the site of use may occur. If a fungal or bacterial infection of the mouth, or — rarely — an allergic skin reaction appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (A90100ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for melasma.
groups.usage: People aged 15 years and over: take 2 tablets at a time, 3 times a day, after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you are taking an oral medicine that contains tranexamic acid; if you are being given thrombin; if you have severe kidney impairment or hepatic coma; if you have thrombosis (cerebral thrombosis, myocardial infarction, thrombophlebitis, pulmonary embolism and the like); or if the user is under 15 years of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you are aged 55 years or over; if you have an allergic constitution; if you are at risk of thrombosis; or if you have kidney impairment or cystinuria.

If you are not sure that the mark is melasma, or if it is dark, uneven in tone or raised above the surface of the skin, consult a dermatologist before taking this medicine. If you are having medical tests, tell the doctor that you are taking a preparation containing vitamin C, because this medicine may affect urine and stool test results.

Do not take this medicine continuously for more than 2 months. If you take it again, leave a gap of at least 2 months.

Do not take this medicine together with tranexamic acid or thrombin. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before using it with oral contraceptives or hormone replacement therapy.

If rash, itching, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, heartburn or early signs of thrombosis (severe headache, slurred speech, a crushing chest pain lasting more than 10 minutes, sudden shortness of breath, pain or swelling in one calf, sudden difficulty breathing of unknown cause, or a temporary loss of consciousness with chest pain) appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (B40900ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills (feeling cold and shivery), fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: There is a daytime product and a night-time product. For the daytime product: ages 7 years to under 15 years take 1 tablet at a time, and people aged 15 years and over take 2 tablets at a time, 2 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. For the night-time product: 6 hours after the daytime product has been taken, ages 7 years to under 15 years take 1 tablet at a time, and people aged 15 years and over take 2 tablets at a time, once a day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take this medicine together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had a reaction to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction to a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if the user is an older person, is debilitated or has a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or have ulcer or bleeding problems; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or have had an allergic reaction to it.

If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take this medicine together with oral medicines that contain an antitussive or expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines). Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants or steroids. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If rash, redness, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, or — rarely — signs of shock (hives, swelling and chest tightness after taking the medicine, together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, redness and burn-like blistering), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice or interstitial pneumonia (cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever and the like) appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (101406ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fever and pain caused by a cold, and for headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, period pain, sprain pain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: Children aged 12 years and under: take the recommended dose 1 time, when needed, every 4 to 6 hours. Take this medicine at the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible period, and do not take it more than 5 times in 1 day (75 mg/kg). If the body weight is known, dosing by body weight (10 to 15 mg/kg) is more appropriate. For ages 4 months to 6 months (body weight 7 to 7.9 kg) the recommended single dose is 1 tablet (80 mg); at 12 years of age (body weight 43 kg and over) the recommended single dose is 8 tablets (640 mg). For the detailed recommended dose for each age group, refer to the approved product information.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so it must not be taken by people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their phenylalanine intake.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take this medicine together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment or severely reduced heart function; if you have aspirin-induced asthma (asthma attacks triggered by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicines) or have had it in the past; if you have taken barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have had a peptic ulcer; if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have abnormal heart function; if you have bronchial asthma; if the user is an older person; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Do not take this medicine together with other anti-inflammatory analgesics, other products containing acetaminophen, barbiturates or tricyclic antidepressants. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with warfarin, lithium or thiazide diuretics.

If signs of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing of the whole body, angioedema, hives, an asthma attack and the like), low platelet count, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, bleeding in the digestive tract, peptic ulcer, perforation, hypersensitivity symptoms (facial swelling, sweating, low blood pressure), rash, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), abnormal liver function such as raised AST or ALT, or a fixed drug eruption appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (A19500ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for diarrhoea, an upset stomach, loose stools and vomiting with diarrhoea.
groups.usage: People aged 15 years and over: take 2 tablets at a time. Ages 8 years to under 15 years: take 1 tablet at a time. Take the dose 3 times a day, leaving an interval of at least 4 hours. Children aged 7 years and under must not take this medicine.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, if the user is a newborn baby or a child aged 7 years or under, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is an older person; if you have diarrhoea with fever, or persistent bloody or mucous stools; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or have had an allergic reaction to it.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Do not take this medicine continuously for more than 1 week.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve period cramps (severe abdominal pain), swelling, headache, low back pain, muscle pain and tiredness.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and over: take 2 tablets at a time with water. When needed, take a dose at intervals of 6 hours, and do not exceed a total of 8 tablets in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take this medicine together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had a reaction to it, if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine, or if you are already taking another medicine that contains acetaminophen.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have a constitution that makes allergy likely or have had allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you are debilitated or have a high fever; if the user is an older person; if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; if you have heart disease, systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Do not take this medicine together with other antipyretic analgesics, other products containing acetaminophen, cold medicines, antitussives and expectorants, antihistamines, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

groups.title: Oral liquid (A13100ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the symptomatic treatment of gastro-oesophageal reflux — acid reflux, heartburn and the indigestion caused by reflux of stomach contents (for example after stomach surgery, as a result of a hiatus hernia, during pregnancy or together with reflux oesophagitis).
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and over: take 1 to 2 sachets (15 to 30 mL) at each of the 4 doses a day (after meals and before going to bed). Children under 12 years of age should take an appropriate amount as directed by a doctor.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are on a sodium-restricted diet, if you have low stomach acid, or if the user is a child under 12 years of age.

If symptoms are not improved after 7 days, consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

If an allergic reaction such as itching, bronchial constriction or an anaphylactic reaction appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Diarrhoea and constipation may occur.

groups.title: Ointment (102935COM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for herpes simplex virus infections (including first-episode and recurrent genital herpes and cold sores on the lips).
groups.usage: Apply to the affected area (the diseased site) 2 to 5 times a day at intervals of 4 hours, for 1 week. If there is no effect after 1 week of use, or if symptoms get worse, change to another form of treatment.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had a reaction to it, if you have chemical intolerance, if you are breast-feeding, or if the user is a child.

Consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are immunodeficient, for example because of AIDS or a bone marrow transplant, or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Start treatment as early as possible; in recurrent infection, start it when the warning symptoms or the first lesions (sore areas) appear. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not use this medicine to prevent infecting other people or to prevent recurrent herpes simplex (blister) infection. Do not use it as a base for diluting or mixing other medicines. Use this medicine externally only. Do not use it in the eyes, on the cornea or on mucous membranes. To keep the medicine from spreading to other parts of the body or infecting other people, apply it while wearing a finger cot or rubber gloves.

Consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are taking or using probenecid.

Discomfort such as tenderness (pain on pressure), a temporary burning feeling, mild pain including stinging, contact dermatitis, an erythematous rash, eczema, allergic reactions and, occasionally, irritation at the site of application, itching, inflammation of the vulva, facial swelling, loss of skin colour, hives, rash, a blistering rash, redness of the skin and itching may occur.

groups.title: Cream (235733CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fungal skin infections caused by dermatophytes (athlete's foot, tinea cruris (jock itch) and tinea corporis), and for pityriasis versicolor caused by Pityrosporum orbiculare and for cutaneous candidiasis.
groups.usage: Apply to the affected area (the diseased site) 1 to 2 times a day. The length of treatment depends on the condition: for athlete's foot (tinea pedis), 1 time a day for 1 week; for the interdigital (between the toes) type of athlete's foot, 2 times a day for 1 week; for the plantar (sole of the foot) type of athlete's foot, 2 times a day for 2 weeks; for tinea corporis and tinea cruris (jock itch), 1 to 2 weeks; for cutaneous candidiasis, 1 to 2 weeks; and for pityriasis versicolor, 2 weeks.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, or if the user is a child.

Do not use an occlusive dressing or wrapping unless a doctor tells you to. If you have candidiasis, do not use acidic soap. Use this medicine externally only.

Do not use it in the eyes, on the cornea or on the conjunctiva. If it gets into the eye by mistake it may irritate the eye and, rarely, a hidden fungal infection may get worse, so rinse the eye thoroughly with plenty of water. Do not use it on the nails, the scalp, around the mouth or in the vaginal area. If symptoms have not improved after the treatment period, consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

If a hypersensitivity reaction with rash, excessive irritation, hives, redness, rash, reddening of the skin, itching, a feeling of irritation, local contact dermatitis, peeling of the skin, scabbing of a wound, abnormal pigmentation, stinging or a burning feeling appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Fungal skin infections (athlete's foot, tinea cruris, tinea corporis), pityriasis versicolor, cutaneous candidiasis

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have heart disease, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are debilitated or have a high fever; if the user is an older person; if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache; if you have symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like); or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.

If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinsonian medicines and the like), other oral medicines for rhinitis, or oral medicines containing an antihistamine (cold medicines, antitussives and expectorants, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines and the like). groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fungal skin infections (ringworm, cutaneous candidiasis, pityriasis versicolor) that are accompanied by clinical signs such as inflammation, itching and eczema.
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (the diseased site) 1 to 2 times a day (in the morning, or in the morning and the evening).
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have a bacterial or viral skin infection; if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine; if you have eczematous otitis externa with a perforated eardrum; if you have an ulcer; if you have a deep second-degree or worse burn or frostbite; if you have perioral dermatitis, common acne, rosacea, syphilis, tuberculosis or a similar skin disease; if you are breast-feeding; or if you have a skin vaccine reaction. Do not apply it to broken skin or over a wide area (10 % or more of the body surface).

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or if the user is a baby or a young child.

Use this medicine externally only; it must not be used internally. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Once the acute symptoms have gone, use a medicine that does not contain a corticosteroid. In babies and young children, avoid using it over a wide area for a long period. Do not use it if symptoms are not improving or are getting worse. Once symptoms improve, stop using it as soon as possible. Do not use an occlusive dressing unless a doctor tells you to; take care, because a nappy and the like can act in the same way as an occlusive dressing. If it is used on the genitals together with latex contraceptives (condoms and vaginal pessaries), it may damage them and reduce their safety and effectiveness.

If a hypersensitivity reaction (occasionally a burning feeling, skin irritation, rash, redness, allergic contact dermatitis, a prickling feeling or swelling) appears, stop using this medicine. Bacterial skin infections (impetigo, folliculitis and the like) may occur.
